title: Prevent unrelated workflow remediation from suppressing Supervisor triage
objective: Fix the bounded identity-matching defect in the EXISTING Automation Intelligent Orchestration plan: row_matches_workflow currently accepts substring matches across workflow, finding, objective, candidate ID and candidate path. This allows a CODEX_READY/IN_REMEDIATION record for a different workflow with a shared substring to falsely route a current RED workflow as FOLLOW_EXISTING_REMEDIATION, suppressing its Luna/Sol diagnosis. Match exact canonical workflow identity (with only a verified, explicit .yml/.yaml/path normalization when appropriate), and preserve existing remediation authority/deduplication. No new router, queue, scheduler or supervisor.

evidence.summary: row_matches_workflow() uses `target in workflow_key(value) or workflow_key(value) in target` for five heterogeneous fields; best_remediation_match() trusts that predicate. build_plan() routes matching active states to FOLLOW_EXISTING_REMEDIATION.
Current tests cover correct exact match, isolated errors, repeated errors, clustering, and fingerprint no-op; no negative collision case for overlapping workflow strings.
Observed return values prove the substring identity defect; this is a synthetic reachable control-flow error, NOT evidence that the current production ETF failure was actually misrouted.
Existing ownership for Automation Production Health and deduped remediation; no parallel agent or independent owner.

reproduction: From exact pinned main 8c4be3fe43b04f79c59cb89b74954fbcf5f1c05c, import row_matches_workflow and build_plan from scripts/framework_intelligence/automation_orchestration_v1.py. The present matcher returns True for unrelated target='daily-settled-etf-calibration.yml' with remediation row {'workflow':'etf.yml','state':'CODEX_READY'}; it also returns True for target='alpha-backup.yml' with row {'workflow':'alpha.yml','state':'IN_REMEDIATION'}. In an otherwise isolated RED health fixture, injecting such an unrelated active remediation record causes build_plan to choose FOLLOW_EXISTING_REMEDIATION instead of Luna/Sol. A same-exact-workflow CODEX_READY row SHOULD still dedupe. Revalidate against fresh main and existing remediation schema before code changes; stop cleanly if superseded/fixed. Does not claim actual current prod ETF false-match.

positive: Matching a CODEX_READY remediation row whose workflow identity is exactly the RED workflow retains FOLLOW_EXISTING_REMEDIATION and consumes zero duplicate model calls.
Supported explicit .yml/.yaml representation or matching canonical path normalization, if confirmed by current source contract, retains true matches without relying on broad substring fields.
When no exact active remediation exists, an isolated RED first failure routes through existing LUNA_TRIAGE; repeated failure/cluster retains existing SOL route.
Run the full existing tests/framework_intelligence/test_automation_orchestration_v1.py plus the new focused tests, and verify only existing output contracts and ownership are used.
negative: A row with workflow etf.yml MUST NOT match daily-settled-etf-calibration.yml; a row with workflow alpha.yml MUST NOT match alpha-backup.yml.

A generic objective/finding/candidate_path/candidate_id merely mentioning or partially containing target workflow text MUST NOT confer a remediation identity if the row's explicit workflow is another value.

A stale/inactive row, missing/ambiguous identity or unrelated candidate MUST NOT suppress RED diagnosis by pretending an existing active repair; preserve UNKNOWN/NEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE where appropriate.

No new supervisor/router/scheduler/remediation queue, no paid model calls, no automatic merge, no override of CODEX_READY authority, no historical receipt rewriting, no market or portfolio behavior changes.
